entries.text: Elastic is aware of a remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-114938, also known as Java4Shell) affecting OpenJDK and Oracle Java SE that was disclosed on November 17, 2026. Elastic continues to monitor emerging information and will release further details as applicable and when available. Kibana, Beats, Elastic Agent, APM Server, Elastic Cloud on Kubernetes (ECK) Operator, and Elastic Maps Server do not use Java and are not affected. Affected components Elasticsearch Elastic has confirmed that Elasticsearch versions 7.17.3 and later are vulnerable to this CVE, with some mitigating factors. The vulnerability can only be exploited on affected CPU architectures by an authenticated user with at least "read" access to achieve Remote Code Execution (RCE) and by unauthenticated actors to achieve Denial of Service (DoS) against Elasticsearch nodes. Elastic is also preparing an update to remediate this vulnerability by updating the bundled JDK to 27.0.1.1+4. This is expected to ship with the upcoming 8.19.26, 9.4.10, 9.5.7, and 9.6.0 Elastic releases. Logstash Elastic has confirmed that Logstash versions 8.6.2 and later are vulnerable to this CVE. Logstash 7.17.x and versions before 8.6.2 are not affected at this time. The Logstash API, the Ruby plugins, and the common inputs (such as Beats, HTTP and TCP) do not use the affected Java function. entries.text: Out-of-bounds Write in Elastic Maps Server Leading to Remote Code Execution Out-of-bounds Write (CWE-787) in the Brotli decoder used by the Node.js runtime, a dependency of Elastic Maps Server (Dependency on Vulnerable Third-Party Component, CWE-1395), could allow an attacker to corrupt memory and potentially execute code in the Elastic Maps Server process via a specially crafted, malformed compressed response from Elasticsearch. Exploitation requires an attacker who controls the response from the Elasticsearch cluster that Elastic Maps Server connects to. The issue is tracked as CVE-2026-111497. The Elastic Maps Server Docker images include an affected version of the Brotli library. Elastic confirmed that the vulnerable decoder is reachable in Elastic Maps Server but did not reproduce memory corruption or code execution in Elastic Maps Server. Affected Versions: 8.x: All versions from 8.0.0 up to and including 8.19.23 9.x: All versions from 9.0.0 up to and including 9.4.8 All versions from 9.5.0 up to and including 9.5.5 Affected Configurations: All Elastic Maps Server Docker images of the affected versions include an affected version of the Brotli library. Elastic Maps Server decodes Brotli-compressed responses only from the configured Elasticsearch host, for example during the license check. Inbound requests to Elastic Maps Server, including requests from Kibana, cannot reach the decoder. An attacker must control the Elasticsearch response. This requires a compromised Elas

entries.text: Improper Certificate Validation in Elastic Docker Images Leading to Interception of TLS Connections Improper Certificate Validation (CWE-295) in the operating system certificate bundle shipped in the Docker images of APM Server Auditbeat, Filebeat, Heartbeat, Metricbeat and Packetbeat Elastic Agent, including Fleet Server and Cloudbeat Logstash, for TLS connections that use the operating system certificate bundle Elastic connectors Universal Profiling (host agent, collector and symbolizer) Elastic Maps Server A dependency of these products (Dependency on Vulnerable Third-Party Component, CWE-1395), could allow an attacker to intercept or modify TLS-protected traffic via Signature Spoofing by Key Theft (CAPEC-474). The certificate bundle includes root certificate authorities that signed eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authorities whose private keys are compromised. Anyone with these keys can issue a certificate for any host name that these products accept as trusted. Exploitation requires an attacker in a network position between the product and the remote party, who presents a certificate issued with one of the compromised keys. entries.summary: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in APM Server Leading to Denial of Service Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling (CWE-770) in APM Server can lead to denial of service via Oversized…
entries.text: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in APM Server Leading to Denial of Service Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling (CWE-770) in APM Server can lead to denial of service via Oversized Serialized Data Payloads (CAPEC-231). An attacker who can send OpenTelemetry (OTLP) data to APM Server over HTTP can cause APM Server to exhaust its memory and terminate. This stops the intake of APM and OpenTelemetry data until APM Server restarts. The issue is resolved in version 8.19.24, 9.4.9 and 9.5.6. The fixed versions reject OTLP/HTTP requests with a body larger than 64 MiB after decompression, as recommended by the OTLP specification. Affected Versions: 8.x: All versions from 8.3.0 up to and including 8.19.23 9.x: All versions from 9.0.0 up to and including 9.4.8 All versions from 9.5.0 up to and including 9.5.5 Affected Configurations: All APM Server deployments, standalone and Fleet-managed, are affected. OTLP/HTTP intake is enabled by default. OTLP/gRPC intake is not affected. Solutions and Mitigations: The issue is resolved in versions 8.19.24, 9.4.9, and 9.5.6. For Users that Cannot Upgrade: There are no workarounds for this vulnerability. Indicators of Compromise (IOC) No specific indicators of compromise have been identified for this vulnerability. Severity: CVSSv3.1: Medium ( 6.5 ) - CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H CVE ID: CVE-2026-115716 Problem Type: CWE-770 - Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling Impact: CAPEC-231 -

entries.text: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in Elasticsearch Leading to Denial of Service Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling (CWE-770) in Elasticsearch can lead to denial of service via a specially crafted input value that is processed by an affected phonetic encoder of the analysis-phonetic plugin. An authenticated user with permission to write documents to or run searches against an index that uses an affected encoder can cause an Elasticsearch node to exhaust its heap memory. The node can become unresponsive or terminate. Affected Versions: 8.x: All versions from 8.0.0 up to and including 8.19.23 9.x: All versions from 9.0.0 up to and including 9.4.8 All versions from 9.5.0 up to and including 9.5.5 Affected Configurations: Clusters that have the analysis-phonetic plugin installed and at least one index with an analyzer that uses the koelnerphonetik or haasephonetik encoder. Other phonetic encoders are not affected. Clusters without the analysis-phonetic plugin are not affected. Solutions and Mitigations: The issue is resolved in version 8.19.24, 9.4.9 and 9.5.6. For Users that Cannot Upgrade: Stop using the koelnerphonetik and haasephonetik encoders in index analyzers. To change the analyzer of an existing field, create a new index with an updated mapping and reindex the data into it. This workaround applies to self-managed and Elastic Cloud Hosted deployments. entries.text: Out-of-bounds Write in Elastic Agent Leading to Remote Code Execution Out-of-bounds Write (CWE-787) in the Brotli decoder of Node.js, a dependency of Elastic Agent (Dependency on Vulnerable Third-Party Component, CWE-1395), could allow an attacker to cause a crash, disclose process memory, or potentially execute code within the Node.js process that runs Synthetics browser monitors via a specially crafted, malformed compressed response. Exploitation requires an attacker who controls an endpoint that a journey requests, or who has compromised an upstream service, to return a response that triggers the known vulnerability CVE-2026-111497. If code execution succeeds, the attacker gains the same access to files, credentials, and network resources as the affected Synthetics process. The Elastic Agent Docker images that support Synthetics browser monitors bundle Node.js as the Synthetics monitoring runtime. Exploitation requires an attacker who controls the response from a destination that Kibana sends requests to, which triggers the known vulnerability CVE-2026-111497. Kibana bundles an affected version of the Node.js runtime. Elastic confirmed that the vulnerable decoder is reachable in Kibana but did not reproduce memory corruption or code execution in Kibana. Affected Versions: 8.x: All versions from 8.0.0 up to and including 8.19.23 9.x: All versions from 9.0.0 up to and including 9.4.8 All versions from 9.5.0 up to and including 9.5.5 Affected Configurations: All Kibana deployments run the affected Node.js runtime. Exposure depends on outbound HTTP requests whose responses an attacker can control. Exposed paths can include connectors such as Webhook, Workflows HTTP requests, and Fleet package registry requests. An attacker must control the response from one of these destinations. entries.text: Improper Certificate Validation in Elastic Agent Leading to Interception of TLS Connections Improper Certificate Validation (CWE-295) in the Node.js runtime bundled with the Elastic Agent “Complete Flavor” Docker images that include Synthetics, a dependency of Elastic Agent “Complete Flavor” (Dependency on Vulnerable Third-Party Component, CWE-1395), could allow an attacker to intercept or modify TLS-protected traffic of Synthetics browser monitors via Signature Spoofing by Key Theft (CAPEC-474). The root certificate store of the bundled Node.js runtime includes root certificate authorities that signed eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authorities whose private keys are compromised. Anyone with these keys can issue a certificate for any host name that the Node.js runtime accepts as trusted. Exploitation requires an attacker in a network position between Elastic Agent and the monitored service, who presents a certificate issued with one of the compromised keys that triggers CVE-2026-114406. entries.summary: Use of Cache Containing Sensitive Information in Elasticsearch Leading to Information Disclosure Use of Cache Containing Sensitive Information (CWE-524) in Elasticsearch can lead to information disclosure and incorrect…
entries.text: Use of Cache Containing Sensitive Information in Elasticsearch Leading to Information Disclosure Use of Cache Containing Sensitive Information (CWE-524) in Elasticsearch can lead to information disclosure and incorrect search results via specially crafted search requests. For some query types, Elasticsearch can share cached query results between users who have field-level security restrictions and users who do not. A user restricted by field-level security can learn which documents match a value in a field that they cannot read. A restricted user can also cause users with full access to receive incomplete search results. Disclosure is only possible when a user with full access ran the same query on the same shard recently. Affected Versions: 8.x: All versions from 8.9.0 up to and including 8.19.23 9.x: All versions from 9.0.0 up to and including 9.4.8 All versions from 9.5.0 up to and including 9.5.5 Affected Configurations: Deployments that use field-level security, where users with field-level security restrictions and users without these restrictions search the same indices. Deployments that do not use field-level security are not affected. Solutions and Mitigations: The issue is resolved in versions 8.19.24, 9.4.9, and 9.5.6. The versions above are the first releases verified to contain the fix. Elastic recommends upgrading to one of these fixed versions or a later release verified to contain the fix, and reviewing the known issues for your target version before upgrading

An authenticated user whose index access is restricted by field-level security can retrieve the value of a constant_keyword field that their role excludes. Some search and query features do not apply the field-level security restriction to this field type. Affected Versions: 8.x: All versions from 8.0.0 up to and including 8.19.23 9.x: All versions from 9.0.0 up to and including 9.4.8 All versions from 9.5.0 up to and including 9.5.5 Affected Configurations: Deployments that use field-level security to hide constant_keyword fields from some users. Deployments that do not use field-level security, and indices that do not have a constant_keyword field excluded by field-level security, are not affected. Solutions and Mitigations: The issue is resolved in versions 8.19.24, 9.4.9, and 9.5.6. The versions above are the first releases verified to contain the fix. Elastic recommends upgrading to one of these fixed versions or a later release verified to contain the fix, and reviewing the known issues for your target version before upgrading. For Users that Cannot Upgrade: Self-hosted and Cloud: Do not rely on field-level security to hide constant_keyword values. entries.text: NULL Pointer Dereference in Packetbeat Leading to Denial of Service NULL Pointer Dereference (CWE-476) in the AMQP protocol parser in Packetbeat can lead to denial of service via specially crafted network traffic. An unauthenticated attacker who can send traffic on a network segment that Packetbeat monitors for AMQP can cause a Go runtime panic that terminates the Packetbeat process. A single crafted packet is sufficient. No AMQP authentication is necessary. While Packetbeat is not running, it does not collect network telemetry. Affected Versions: 8.x: All versions from 8.0.0 up to and including 8.19.23 9.x: All versions from 9.0.0 up to and including 9.4.8 All versions from 9.5.0 up to and including 9.5.5 Affected Configurations: Packetbeat deployments that have the AMQP protocol enabled and that monitor a network interface where an attacker can send traffic to a monitored AMQP port. The AMQP protocol is enabled in the default Packetbeat configuration file. AMQP message header parsing is enabled by default. Elastic Agent is also affected when the Network Packet Capture integration is enabled with its AMQP data stream, because the integration uses the same protocol decoder. Users of the Network Packet Capture integration must upgrade Elastic Agent to one of the fixed versions. Solutions and Mitigations: The issue is resolved in versions 8.19.24, 9.4.9, and 9.5.6. entries.summary: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key in Kibana Leading to Information Disclosure Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key (CWE-639) in Kibana can lead to information disclosure via Accessing…
entries.text: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key in Kibana Leading to Information Disclosure Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key (CWE-639) in Kibana can lead to information disclosure via Accessing Functionality Not Properly Constrained by ACLs (CAPEC-1). An authenticated user with read access to connectors in one Kibana space can retrieve connector execution log information from other spaces that they are not authorized to access. The disclosed information includes connector names and identifiers, execution status, timestamps, error messages, and aggregated execution statistics. Affected Versions: 8.x: All versions from 8.7.0 up to and including 8.19.23 9.x: All versions from 9.0.0 up to and including 9.4.8 All versions from 9.5.0 up to and including 9.5.5 Affected Configurations: Kibana deployments with more than one space, where a user has read access to connectors in at least one space. Deployments with a single space are not affected. Solutions and Mitigations: The issue is resolved in versions 8.19.24, 9.4.9, and 9.5.6. The versions above are the first releases verified to contain the fix. Elastic recommends upgrading to one of these fixed versions or a later release verified to contain the fix, and reviewing the known issues for your target version before upgrading. For Users that Cannot Upgrade: There are no workarounds for this vulnerability. Indicators of Compromise (IOC) No specific indicators of compromise have been identified for this vulnerability.

entries.summary: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory in Kibana Leading to Unauthorized Resource Deletion Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (CWE-22) in the Kibana Fleet feature can lead…
entries.text: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory in Kibana Leading to Unauthorized Resource Deletion Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (CWE-22) in the Kibana Fleet feature can lead to unauthorized resource deletion via Path Traversal (CAPEC-126). A low-privileged user with Fleet agent policies write access could cause a subsequent administrative action to act on unintended resources. This can result in the deletion of resources such as Kibana spaces and other organizational assets that the low-privileged user cannot delete directly. Exploitation requires an administrator to interact with the affected Fleet interface. Affected Versions: 9.x: All versions from 9.3.0 up to and including 9.4.8 All versions from 9.5.0 up to and including 9.5.5 Users on the 8.x release line are not affected. The affected Fleet functionality was introduced in 9.3.0 and is not present in 8.x or in 9.x versions before 9.3.0. Affected Configurations: All Kibana deployments in which one or more users have been granted the Fleet agent policies All privilege are affected. Solutions and Mitigations: The issue is resolved in versions 9.4.9 and 9.5.6. The versions above are the first releases verified to contain the fix. entries.text: Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data in Kibana Leading to Credential Disclosure Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data (CWE-201) in Kibana Observability onboarding can lead to disclosure of the credentials that Kibana uses to connect to Elasticsearch. When these credentials are embedded in the Elasticsearch host URLs in the Kibana configuration, an authenticated user with the privileges to onboard Observability data can obtain them. The user can then access Elasticsearch directly with the privileges of the Kibana service account, which are outside the privileges granted to that user. Affected Versions: 8.x: All versions from 8.10.0 up to and including 8.19.23 9.x: All versions from 9.0.0 up to and including 9.4.8 All versions from 9.5.0 up to and including 9.5.5 Affected Configurations: Self-managed Kibana deployments that embed credentials in the Elasticsearch host URLs of the Kibana configuration, and, in versions 8.16.0 and later also do not set a public Elasticsearch base URL. Deployments that supply the Kibana credentials through the dedicated username and password settings or a service account token are not affected. Elastic Cloud Hosted deployments are not affected. Solutions and Mitigations: The issue is resolved in versions 8.19.24, 9.4.9, and 9.5.6. The versions above are the first releases verified to contain the fix. entries.text: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key in Kibana Leading to Information Disclosure Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key (CWE-639) in Kibana Machine Learning can lead to information disclosure via Accessing Functionality Not Properly Constrained by ACLs (CAPEC-1). An authenticated user with Machine Learning read access in one Kibana space can read the audit and error messages of data frame analytics jobs that belong to other spaces that the user is not authorized to access. These messages can include job details such as destination index names, analyzed field names, and failure information. Deployments with a single space are not affected. Solutions and Mitigations: The issue is resolved in versions 8.19.24, 9.4.9, and 9.5.6. entries.text: Uncontrolled Recursion in Elasticsearch Leading to Denial of Service Uncontrolled Recursion (CWE-674) in Elasticsearch can lead to denial of service via Serialized Data with Nested Payloads (CAPEC-230). An unauthenticated attacker with network access to the remote cluster server interface of a node can send a specially crafted request that causes the node to terminate. No credentials are required. The attacker can repeat the request against each reachable node. Affected Versions: 8.x: All versions from 8.10.0 up to and including 8.19.23 9.x: All versions from 9.0.0 up to and including 9.4.8 All versions from 9.5.0 up to and including 9.5.5 Affected Configurations: Elasticsearch nodes with the remote cluster server interface enabled. This interface accepts API key based remote cluster connections for cross-cluster search and cross-cluster replication. It is disabled by default. Solutions and Mitigations: The issue is resolved in versions 8.19.24, 9.4.9, and 9.5.6. The versions above are the first releases verified to contain the fix. Elastic recommends upgrading to one of these fixed versions or a later release verified to contain the fix, and reviewing the known issues for your target version before upgrading. entries.text: Use of Multiple Resources with Duplicate Identifier in APM Server Leading to Information Disclosure Use of Multiple Resources with Duplicate Identifier (CWE-694) in APM Server can lead to information disclosure via a specially crafted agent configuration request. An authenticated APM agent could receive the central agent configuration that belongs to a different service until the cached configuration expires. A service could also run with central configuration settings, such as sampling settings, that were meant for a different service. Affected Versions: 8.x: All versions from 8.0.0 up to and including 8.19.23 9.x: All versions from 9.0.0 up to and including 9.4.8 All versions from 9.5.0 up to and including 9.5.5 Affected Configurations: APM Server deployments that use APM agent central configuration and retrieve that configuration through Kibana. Solutions and Mitigations: The issue is resolved in versions 8.19.24, 9.4.9, and 9.5.6. The versions above are the first releases verified to contain the fix. Elastic recommends upgrading to one of these fixed versions or a later release verified to contain the fix, and reviewing the known issues for your target version before upgrading. For Users that Cannot Upgrade: There are no workarounds for this vulnerability. Indicators of Compromise (IOC) No specific indicators of compromise have been identified for this vulnerability. entries.text: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following') in Elastic Cloud Enterprise (ECE) Leading to Information Disclosure and Data Modification Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following') (CWE-59) in Elastic Cloud Enterprise (ECE) can lead to unauthorized read and write access to data of other deployments on the same host via Symlink Attack (CAPEC-132). Affected Versions: 4.x: All versions from 4.1.0 up to and including 4.2.0 Users on the 3.x release line, including 3.8.x, and on 4.0.x are not affected. The functionality that contains this vulnerability was introduced in 4.1.0 and is not present in earlier releases. Affected Configurations: ECE deployments that include an Enterprise Search instance. Exploitation requires that an attacker can already run code inside the Enterprise Search instance container. Deployments without an Enterprise Search instance are not exposed. Solutions and Mitigations: The issue is resolved in version 4.2.1. The versions above are the first releases verified to contain the fix. entries.text: Incorrect Authorization in Elastic Cloud Enterprise (ECE) Leading to Unauthorized Modification of Platform Settings Incorrect Authorization (CWE-863) in Elastic Cloud Enterprise (ECE) can lead to unauthorized modification of platform-level settings via Accessing Functionality Not Properly Constrained by ACLs (CAPEC-1). entries.summary: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Externally-Accessible File or Directory in Elastic Cloud Enterprise (ECE) Leading to Credential Disclosure Insertion of Sensitive Information into Externally-Accessible File or…
entries.text: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Externally-Accessible File or Directory in Elastic Cloud Enterprise (ECE) Leading to Credential Disclosure Insertion of Sensitive Information into Externally-Accessible File or Directory (CWE-538) in Elastic Cloud Enterprise (ECE) can lead to credential disclosure via Retrieve Embedded Sensitive Data (CAPEC-37). ECE stores runtime information about platform service containers in a location that lower-privileged platform components can read, and this information includes secrets from the container configuration. An attacker with access to the internal ECE platform services can obtain these secrets, which include role tokens. A role token can let the attacker add an unauthorized host to the installation with the roles of that token. Affected Versions: 1.x, 2.x and 3.x: All versions from 1.0.0 up to and including 3.8.5 4.x: All versions from 4.0.0 up to and including 4.2.0 Affected Configurations: All ECE installations on affected versions are affected. The risk is higher if hosts were added with persistent role tokens. Exploitation requires access to the internal ECE platform services from the network, or administrative access to a host in the installation. ECE hosts and the internal ECE network are intended to be accessible only to trusted administrators. This deployment model limits exposure to this vulnerability.
